name: PatchMerger
backbones: ViT-S/32; ViT-B/32; ViT-L/32; ViT-L/16; ViT-H/14; ViT-H/11; V-MoE (S/32 to H/14)
main_result: ViT-H/14 (JFT-300M pretraining): same JFT precision@1 and ImageNet 10-shot accuracy as ViT-H/14 at 51.6% of the FLOPs and 63.5% of the runtime
notes: A single merger after the first half of the blocks maps any number of input tokens to a fixed M=8 output tokens: each patch gets M scores from a learned linear map, softmax over the scores, and the outputs are the score-weighted sums (fixed learned queries, like TokenLearner). Trained from scratch on JFT-300M, then few-shot or fully fine-tuned on ImageNet; no DeiT-S and no ImageNet-1k-only training. Runtime is reported as total training runtime (appendix figures), hardware not stated in the text.
evidence: "outputs a fixed number of tokens when applied to any number of input tokens" (Sec. 3); "computes M scores s1:M (p) — one per output patch — based on a linear transformation of the patch representation at that point" (Sec. 3); "we place one merger layer in the middle of the network, and it outputs 8 patches" (Sec. 4); "We train all of our models on JFT (Hinton et al., 2015), a proprietary dataset containing 300M images." (Sec. 4)

name: TCFormer
backbones: TCFormer (own 4-stage architecture); TCFormer-Light
main_result: TCFormer: ImageNet-1k top-1 82.4 at 5.9 GFLOPs (25.6M params; DeiT-S 79.9 at 4.6); COCO-WholeBody whole-body AP 57.2
notes: New hierarchical architecture, not a plug-in. The CTM block between stages clusters tokens with DPC-KNN on token features and merges each cluster by an importance-weighted average (importance score P predicted from the features), then merged tokens attend to the original ones. Cluster number fixed to a quarter of the input tokens per stage. ImageNet model trained from scratch for 300 epochs. No DeiT-S results. No latency numbers; the paper only says clustering and merging take 9.4% of the forward time and that DPC-KNN is quadratic in the token number.
evidence: "which merges tokens by progressive clustering, where the tokens can be merged from different locations with flexible shapes and sizes" (Abstract); "we utilize a variant of k-nearest neighbor based density peaks clustering algorithm (DPC-KNN)" (Sec. 3.3); "we set the cluster number to a quarter of the input token number" (Sec. 3.5); "TCFormer without the MTA head is trained from scratch for 300 epochs" (Sec. 4.4)

name: Token Pooling
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-e318; DeiT-e252; DeiT-Ti
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 80.6 at 2.6 GFLOPs with WK-Medoids (baseline DeiT-S retrained by the authors 81.2 at 4.6)
notes: K-Means or K-Medoids clustering of the tokens after each block, output = cluster centres; the optional weights and the centre initialisation use the significance score (total attention received by a token, PoWER-BERT style), so the criterion is feature similarity plus an attention statistic. The number of retained tokens per layer K is found offline with PoWER-BERT's soft-selection stage and is the same for every image. Main results fine-tune DeiT after inserting the pooling layers (training protocol in Sec. 5); Appendix E reports the no-fine-tuning case, where carrying the cluster counts into the softmax preserves the most accuracy. The abstract's 42% fewer computations refers to DeiT-Ti. GFLOPs include the clustering cost. No throughput or latency reported.
evidence: "It downsamples input tokens via clustering the tokens and returns the cluster centers (the average of the tokens in a cluster)." (Sec. 4); "A good choice of the weights is the significance scores (5), i.e., wi = si ." (Sec. 4); "we use the automatic search procedure proposed by Goyal et al. (2020) to determine K" (Appendix G); "(3) We further finetune the downsampling methods using K." (Sec. 5); "we evaluate the performance when we insert Token Pooling layers into a pre-trained model without finetuning" (Appendix E)

name: PaCa-ViT
backbones: PaCa-Tiny; PaCa-Small; PaCa-Base; PaCa-mlp-Small; PaCa-ec-Small/Base (own PVTv2-style architecture)
main_result: PaCa-Small: ImageNet-1k top-1 83.08 at 5.5 GFLOPs (22.0M params; PVTv2-B2 82.0 at 3.9; DeiT-S 79.9 at 4.6)
notes: New architecture. In each PaCa block the keys and values come from M=100 learned soft clusters (cluster assignment C from a depth-wise conv or MLP module with softmax over the spatial dimension; Z = LayerNorm(C^T X)), while queries stay per patch, so attention is linear in N; the number of clusters is a fixed hyper-parameter per stage. Trained from scratch 300 epochs with the DeiT/PVTv2 recipe. At 224px the FLOPs are higher than the PVTv2 baselines; gains appear at high resolution (detection, segmentation). No DeiT-S plug-in results, no latency.
evidence: "Queries in our PaCa-ViT starts with patches, while keys and values are directly based on clustering (with a predefined small number of clusters). The clusters are learned end-to-end" (Abstract); "a predefined number M of clusters (e.g., M = 100), we first compute the cluster assignment CN,M" (Sec. 3.2); "are trained for 300 epochs from scratch on 10 A100 GPUs" (Appendix)

name: ToMe
backbones: ViT-S/B/L (AugReg); ViT-L/H (SWAG); ViT-B/L/H (MAE); DeiT-Ti; DeiT-S; ViT-L (spatiotemporal MAE, Kinetics-400); ViT-B (AudioMAE)
main_result: DeiT-S trained from scratch with ToMe r=13: top-1 79.4 at 2.7 GFLOPs, 1552 im/s (baseline 79.8 at 4.6, 930 im/s); off-the-shelf AugReg ViT-S r=13: 79.3 at 2.7 GFLOPs, 1550 im/s
notes: Bipartite soft matching: tokens split into two sets by alternation, each token in A linked to its most similar token in B by cosine similarity of the attention keys (averaged over heads), the r most similar edges merged by size-weighted averaging; placed between attention and MLP; proportional attention adds log(size) to the logits. Fixed r per block for every image (constant or decreasing schedule). Works off-the-shelf without training; training with ToMe reduces the drop (MAE fine-tuning, DeiT trained from scratch 300 epochs). The DeiT-S row in Table 4 is trained from scratch, not fine-tuned. Throughput on a V100, fp32, optimal batch size. 'other' target = audio (AudioSet).
evidence: "a simple method to increase the throughput of existing ViT models without needing to train" (Abstract); "In each block of a transformer, we merge tokens to reduce by r per layer." (Sec. 3); "we use a dot product similarity metric (e.g., cosine similarity) between the keys of each token to determine which contain similar information" (Sec. 3); "our method works with or without training" (Sec. 1)

name: Quadformer
backbones: ViT-S (DeiT-S architecture); ViT-B; ViT-L
main_result: ViT-B Quadformer (feature-based scorer, 100 patches): top-1 83.05 at 8.9 GMACs, 1435 im/s (vanilla ViT-B with 100 patches 82.31 at 8.8 GMACs, 1739 im/s; 196 patches 84.07 at 17.6 GMACs)
notes: Mixed-resolution tokenizer: a saliency-based Quadtree splits the 256px image into 64/32/16 px patches, all resized to 16px and embedded with 2D position embeddings; the number of patches is fixed by the number of splits. The feature-based scorer uses a frozen ImageNet ShuffleNetV2x0.5 (342K params), so no module is trained for scoring; pixel-blur and Grad-CAM-oracle scorers are also tested. Quadformers are fine-tuned from the base ViTs (130 epochs for ViT-S). DeiT-S cells are for the authors' own ViT-Small (DeiT-S architecture trained from scratch at 256px with 2D sinusoidal position embeddings, 80.28 at 4.62 GMACs with 196 patches): Quadformer with 100 patches gives 78.64 at 2.37 GMACs and 2766 im/s versus vanilla 100 patches 77.55 at 2.28 GMACs and 4212 im/s, so the scorer overhead makes small models slower at equal patch count. Throughput on one RTX 3090, mixed precision, batch 512 (Appendix Table A1).
evidence: "Using the Quadtree algorithm and a novel saliency scorer, we construct a patch mosaic where low-saliency areas of the image are processed in low resolution" (Abstract); "we control the number of patches by setting the number of splits done by the Quadtree algorithm" (Sec. 4.2); "we use a ShuffleNetV2x0.5 [21] model trained on ImageNet-1K as the feature extractor" (Sec. 4.2); "We use the base models to initialize the weights of all our fine-tuned models" (Sec. 4.2)

name: MSViT
backbones: DeiT-S; ViT-Ti; ViT-S; ViT-L (ImageNet-21k AugReg); Swin-T/S/L; Segmenter ViT-Ti/S (ADE20k); EViT and DynamicViT on DeiT-S
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.38 at 4.08 GMACs (average over the val set, 173 tokens; baseline 79.85 at 4.60 GMACs); at matched cost MSDeiT-S 78.76 at 3.32 GMACs vs DeiT-S at 192px 77.79
notes: A 4-layer MLP gate on every 32px coarse region decides, before the first transformer block, whether the region is tokenised at 32px (one token) or 16px (four tokens), so the token count varies per image; gate uses Gumbel-sigmoid with a straight-through estimator and is trained jointly with the backbone for 20 epochs under a generalised batch-shaping sparsity loss (target g*, weight lambda sweep gives several budgets). MACs are averages over the validation set. Latency per image on CPU and GPU (RTX 2080 Ti; V100 for segmentation) in Appendix Table 3 is estimated with the deepspeed library and the batch size is not stated. Only the batch-shaping loss code is released (github.com/Qualcomm-AI-research/batchshaping). Gate transfers frozen to Segmenter, EViT, DynamicViT and Swin.
evidence: "Our method introduces a conditional gating mechanism that selects the optimal token scale for every image region, such that the number of tokens is dynamically determined per input." (Abstract); "Each coarse region is processed by a small 4-layer MLP, the gate g, outputting a binary decision on whether the region should be processed at a coarse or fine scale." (Fig. 2 caption); "We jointly train the transformer and the gate" (Sec. 2.2); "finetune all models for 20 epochs with a batch size of 512 on a single device" (Sec. 4.1)

name: LTMP
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; ViT-T/S/B (AugReg, appendix)
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.6 at 3.0 GFLOPs after one fine-tuning epoch (baseline 79.9 at 4.6); 79.8 at 3.8 GFLOPs
notes: Between attention and MLP of every block: a learned threshold on the importance score (mean column attention, class attention also tested) decides pruning and a second learned threshold on ToMe's key similarity decides merging, so the number of removed tokens varies per image and per layer; merging dominates early layers, pruning late layers. Only two scalars per block are trained (straight-through estimator) for a single epoch with a FLOPs-target loss, backbone frozen. Inference needs batch size 1. FLOPs counted as multiply-adds. Mobile latency on a Google Pixel 7: DeiT-S 212 ms -> LTMP 107 ms at 2.3 GFLOPs (78.6%), ToMe 118 ms (76.9%). No GPU throughput.
evidence: "LTMP uses learned threshold masking modules that dynamically determine which tokens to merge and which to prune." (Abstract); "only tokens with an importance score above the threshold are kept" (Sec. 3.3.1); "We therefore only update the thresholds during training and keep all other trainable parameters fixed, allowing LTMP to converge within a single epoch." (Sec. 3.4.2); "Our learned thresholds approach requires a batch size of 1 during inference as each image is reduced differently." (Sec. 4.7)

name: DiffRate
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-B; ViT-B/L/H (MAE); LV-ViT-S
main_result: DeiT-S off-the-shelf with learned rates: top-1 79.58 at 2.9 GFLOPs, 6744 img/s (baseline 79.82 at 4.6, 5039 img/s); with 30-epoch fine-tuning 79.83
notes: Per block, tokens are sorted by class attention; the N*alpha_p least important are pruned and the next N*(alpha_m - alpha_p) are merged into similar remaining tokens by cosine similarity. The pruning and merging rates per block are learned in 3 epochs with a differentiable discrete proxy (learnable probabilities over candidate rates, attention masking, FLOPs loss) while the backbone is frozen; 1,000 images suffice. The learned rates are then fixed, so every image keeps the same number of tokens (batchable). Reported off-the-shelf and with optional 30-epoch fine-tuning (dagger rows). Throughput on an A100 at batch 1024, fp16. Table 3 also gives latency and power on a Gemmini accelerator for a co-searched variant (batch not stated).
evidence: "by applying the learned layer-wise compression rates to an off-the-shelf ViT-H (MAE) model, we achieve a 40% FLOPs reduction and a 1.5x throughput improvement, with a minor accuracy drop of 0.16% on ImageNet without fine-tuning" (Abstract); "we set fc = fm o fp , meaning that tokens are first pruned and then merged" (Sec. 3); "we employ the class attention Ac in R1xN as the importance metric following EViT [21]" (Sec. 4.1); "We initialize the backbone models with pre-trained models and fix them to train the learnable probabilities in DDP" (Sec. 6.1); "We also fine-tune the model optionally for 30 epochs" (Sec. 6.1)

name: PPT
backbones: DeiT-Ti; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; LV-ViT-S; T2T-ViT; PS-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S fine-tuned 30 epochs: top-1 79.8 at 2.9 GFLOPs, 1448 img/s (baseline 79.8 at 4.6, 993 img/s); off-the-shelf 79.5 at 2.9 GFLOPs
notes: At layers 4, 7 and 10 of DeiT a fixed Top-K number of tokens is removed, but the policy is chosen per instance and layer: if the variance of the ATS-style importance scores (class attention times value norm) exceeds a threshold tau the inattentive tokens are pruned, otherwise similar tokens are pooled with ToMe's bipartite soft matching (size tracking and proportional attention). No trainable parameters; both off-the-shelf and 30-epoch fine-tuned results. Throughput on a single V100 at batch 256. Mirror code also at github.com/mindspore-lab/models.
evidence: "By heuristically integrating both token pruning and token pooling techniques in ViTs without additional trainable parameters" (Abstract); "we propose an adaptive strategy that takes into account both the instances and layers" (Sec. 3.4); "we return to the traditional Top-K selection policy for more controllable compression ratio" (Sec. 3.2); "we report the performance of our method in terms of both off-the-shelf and fine-tuned" (Sec. 4)

name: ToFu
backbones: ViT-B/L (MAE); ViT-S (AugReg); Stable Diffusion v1.5
main_result: ViT-B (MAE, off-the-shelf, r=8): top-1 83.22 at 13.12 GFLOPs, 413.9 im/s with MLERP (ToMe 82.86 at 413.7 im/s; full model 83.74 at 17.58 GFLOPs, 323.6 im/s)
notes: Same bipartite soft matching as ToMe (key similarity, fixed r per layer), but in layers l < d (d=6) the matched source tokens are simply dropped ('pruned merging', faster) and in later layers they are averaged with norm-preserving MLERP (normalised mean scaled by the max norm); choice motivated by the measured functional linearity of the MLPs. Evaluated off-the-shelf (the paper says training is optional but reports none). DeiT-S itself is not run: Table 4 lists ToFu on AugReg ViT-S r=13 at 79.6% / 2.7 GFLOPs / 1561 img/s next to ToMe's DeiT-S numbers. Throughput on V100, fp32. Also applied to Stable Diffusion (FID, LPIPS, time per image). No code URL in the paper.
evidence: "ToFu is versatile, applicable to ViTs with or without additional training." (Abstract); "Central to its operation is the Bipartite Soft Matching (BSM) algorithm [3], which discerns the top r token pairs based on their mutual similarity." (Sec. 3); "early layers use pruned merging, while later layers transition to average (or MLERP) merging" (Fig. 2 caption); "For classification, the settings align with ToMe [3], with token numbers linearly decaying by factor r." (Sec. 4)

name: MCTF
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; T2T-ViT-14/19; LV-ViT-S
main_result: DeiT-S fine-tuned 30 epochs with r=16: top-1 80.1 at 2.6 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6); without training 79.2 at 2.6 GFLOPs
notes: Bidirectional bipartite soft matching with an attraction score that multiplies three criteria: cosine similarity, informativeness (inverse of the mean attention each token receives, taken from the one-step-ahead attention of the next layer and then aggregated for the fused tokens) and inverse token size; fused by attention- and size-weighted average; proportional attention. A fixed r=16 tokens per layer. Fine-tuned 30 epochs with a token-reduction-consistency loss between r and a random r' (no mixup); Table 3 and Appendix Table D give results without any training (the model finetuned at r=16 is also evaluated at other r). Only FLOPs reported, no throughput or latency.
evidence: "a Multi-criteria Token Fusion (MCTF), that gradually fuses the tokens based on multi-criteria (i.e., similarity, informativeness, and size of fused tokens)" (Abstract); "we measure the averaged attention scores a in [0, 1]^N in the self-attention layer, which indicates the impact of each token on others" (Sec. 3.2); "MCTF is applicable with pre-trained ViTs without any additional training since MCTF does not require any learnable parameters" (Sec. 4.1); "we finetune the model with the pre-trained weights for 30 epochs" (Appendix A)

name: PiToMe
backbones: DeiT-T/S/B; ViT-L/H (MAE); CLIP; ALBEF; BLIP; BLIP-2; LLaVA-1.5 7B/13B; BERT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.1 off-the-shelf and 79.8 after retraining at 2.9 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6); ViT-H (MAE) off-the-shelf 86.4 at 92.8 GFLOPs (baseline 86.9 at 167.4)
notes: Energy score per token = mean over the key-token graph of an ELU-like function of cosine similarity with a layer-dependent margin m; the 2k highest-energy tokens are mergeable, the rest protected; the mergeable set is split by sorted energy (odd/even) into A and B and matched by BSM; proportional attention. A fixed ratio r of tokens is kept per layer (k = N - N r). Both off-the-shelf and retrained settings; deits_top1 is the off-the-shelf value, retrained 79.8. Latency only as relative speed-ups and inference times for retrieval and LLaVA (five V100 / A100), no DeiT-S throughput. Also text classification with BERT.
evidence: "This score identifies large clusters of similar tokens as high-energy, indicating potential candidates for merging, while smaller (unique and isolated) clusters are considered as low-energy and preserved." (Abstract); "We opt for using the key vectors K = Xl WK in RNxh as node features of V" (Sec. 3.2); "r is the fraction of remaining tokens" (Sec. 3.1); "We focus on two settings: Off-the-Shelf Performance , where we evaluate the models' performance immediately after compression without training, and Retrained" (Sec. 4)

name: DTEM
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-B; MAE-B; MAE-L; LV-ViT-S; DeiT-T; ViT-S (AugReg, 384px); GIT-B/L (captioning); Segmenter-S (ADE20K)
main_result: DeiT-S end-to-end (30 epochs): top-1 79.85 at 2.9 GFLOPs, 1991 im/s (baseline 79.83 at 4.64, 1390 im/s); modular with frozen backbone 79.44 at 2.91 GFLOPs, 1991 im/s
notes: A lightweight per-block linear embedding (output dim 64, <1% of parameters), decoupled from the ViT features, produces the similarity used by ToMe-style bipartite matching; it is trained through a continuous relaxation (soft top-k grouping and soft merging) with the task loss. 'mixed' here means two trained variants, not training-free: modular (only the embedding trained, backbone frozen = light) or end-to-end (backbone fine-tuned with alternating updates). Inference uses hard BSM with a fixed r per block and proportional attention; a model trained at r=16 generalises to smaller r. Throughput on one RTX 3090, batch 128, fp32.
evidence: "Our method introduces a lightweight embedding module decoupled from the ViT forward pass to extract dedicated features for token merging" (Abstract); "trained either modularly by learning only the decoupled embeddings or end-to-end by fine-tuning" (Abstract); "we employ a uniform reduction strategy, where the reduction rate r represents the number of tokens removed in each transformer block" (Sec. 4.1); "we employ BSM to speed up the inference" (Sec. 3.4)

name: ToCom
backbones: DeiT-B; DeiT-S; ViT-B (MAE)
main_result: DeiT-B on VTAB-1k: a model fine-tuned without ToMe (source r=0) and run with ToMe r=16 (1.9x inference speedup) gains +2.1/+3.6/+1.2 average accuracy on the Natural/Specialized/Structured groups when ToCom is plugged in
notes: Not a new reduction rule: the compression is ToMe (fixed r per layer, key similarity, bipartite soft matching) or EViT. ToCom is a set of LoRA plugins (16 groups, 1.2M params for DeiT-B, h=2 on Wq/Wv) trained once on ImageNet for 10 epochs by self-distillation between random source/target compression degrees with the whole backbone frozen; at inference the plugins are added or subtracted to any downstream fine-tuned model so that it can run at a different r without re-tuning. Evaluated on CIFAR100, 4 FGVC datasets and VTAB-1k; DeiT-S only on VTAB-1k (Table 9), no ImageNet-1k accuracy. Throughput of DeiT-B versus r in Fig. 3 (batch 256 inference, GPU not stated); training on 8xV100.
evidence: "we additionally perform a fast parameter-efficient self-distillation stage on the pre-trained models to obtain a small plugin, called Token Compensator (ToCom), which describes the gap between models across different compression degrees" (Abstract); "It leverages the keys of patch tokens to evaluate their similarity, and merges r similar ones with Bipartite Soft Matching." (Sec. 3.1); "we freeze all pre-trained parameters including the classification heads, and only update the parameter-efficient ToCom" (Sec. 4.2)

name: VoMix
backbones: ViT-B/L/H (MAE); ViT-B@384, ViT-L@512, ViT-H@518 (SWAG); DeiT-S; ViT-S (AugReg); VideoMAE ViT-S/B/L/H (K400, SSV2)
main_result: ViT-H (MAE) off-the-shelf, r=(5%)12: top-1 86.5 at 104.0 GFLOPs, 57 im/s (baseline 86.9 at 167.4, 36 im/s); DeiT-S off-the-shelf 78.6 at 2.9 GFLOPs, fine-tuned 100 epochs 79.6
notes: Inside attention: each token votes for its most similar token (cosine similarity of head-averaged keys), the N*r tokens with the largest weighted vote sum are selected, their queries are mixed into the retained queries by softmax-weighted averaging, and attention is computed with the mixed queries against the full keys/values with proportional attention. The pruning ratio r per layer is a fixed hyper-parameter (constant or decreasing schedule). Parameter-free and applied off-the-shelf; deits_top1 is the training-free DeiT-S value with r=(10% decreasing)12, fine-tuning from DeiT-S for 100 epochs gives 79.6 (and AugReg ViT-S 79.5 off-the-shelf). Throughput on a 32GB V100 at batch 32, reported for MAE/SWAG and video models, not for DeiT-S. No code URL in the paper.
evidence: "a plug-and-play and parameter-free token reduction method, which can be readily applied to off-the-shelf ViT models without any training" (Abstract); "identifying tokens with high homogeneity through a layer-wise token similarity voting mechanism. Subsequently, the selected tokens are mixed into the retained set" (Abstract); "At each layer, with an initial token count of N , VoMix first selects N · r tokens with high homogeneity via token voting." (Sec. Vote&Mix); "we fine-tune VoMix from DeiT-S for 100 epochs" (Sec. Image Experiments)

name: ATM
backbones: DeiT-T/S/B; LV-ViT-T/S; T2T-ViT-14/19; ViT-B (MAE)
main_result: DeiT-S training-free: top-1 79.8 at 3.2 GFLOPs (-30% FLOPs, no accuracy drop) and 79.7 at 3.0 GFLOPs; with 30-epoch fine-tuning 79.8 at 2.6 GFLOPs
notes: Bipartite matching on key similarity, but a pair is merged only if its cosine similarity exceeds a layer-dependent threshold theta_l = max(alpha - (e^{beta(l-1)} - 1), theta_min) (high in early layers, lower later), so the number of merged pairs varies per layer and per image; for batched inference the number merged r_{B,l} is the batch average of pairs above the threshold (Appendix Table A1 shows accuracy/FLOPs for batch sizes 1 to 1024). In the last quarter of the layers tokens are grouped by merging size ('size-distinctive matching') so that two large merged tokens are not combined. Proportional attention; the last layer keeps only the CLS token. Training-free main results plus optional 30-epoch fine-tuning (11 GPU hours). No throughput or latency reported; no code URL in the paper.
evidence: "ATM adaptively reduces tokens across layers and batches by carefully adjusting layer-specific similarity thresholds" (Abstract); "we merge token pairs that are truly similar enough based on the threshold for each layer, instead of a fixed number of pairs with the highest similarity" (Sec. 3.2); "We merge tokens based on the similarity of key pairs for all models." (Appendix A); "training-free ATM achieves over a 30% reduction in FLOPs for the DeiT-T and DeiT-S models without any drop in their original accuracy" (Abstract)

name: Token Transforming
backbones: DeiT-S; ViT-Ti/S/B (AugReg); ViT-H (MAE); T2T-ViT-14; PS-ViT-B; LV-ViT-S; Segmenter-L (ADE20k, Cityscapes); DPT (NYUv2); DINO Swin-L (COCO); LLaVA-1.5-7B
main_result: DeiT-S training-free (/0.7): top-1 79.7 at 3.0 GFLOPs, 1451 im/s (baseline 79.8 at 4.6, 974 im/s); fine-tuned 30 epochs 79.9 at 3.0 GFLOPs and 79.7 at 2.6 GFLOPs (1633 im/s)
notes: Token reduction written as Y = W X with a many-to-many matrix (pruning = diagonal, merging = block-wise are special cases): the M most informative tokens (column sums of the attention map, so no class token is needed) are the targets, each original token contributes to every target by a gated cosine similarity (threshold kappa) normalised with a temperature softmax over targets and then row-normalised, and a continuous size vector rescales the attention logits. The reserving ratio per transforming layer is fixed (0.7 at the usual DeiT layers). Training-free main results plus 30-epoch fine-tuning. Nearest-neighbour token recovery for dense heads. Throughput on a V100 (batch size not stated). No code URL in the paper. 'resample' chosen because every new token is a weighted sum over all old tokens rather than an exclusive group.
evidence: "we propose a many-to-many Token Transforming framework that serves as a generalization of all existing methods and reserves the most information, even enabling training-free acceleration" (Abstract); "We then select the M most informative tokens X s to construct subset Ds from full token set D based on sorting." (Sec. 3.2); "we calculate cosine similarity between informative tokens and full tokens" (Sec. 3.3); "We set reserving ratio to 0.7 by default unless otherwise stated." (Sec. 4.1)

name: DyMU
backbones: CLIP ViT-L/14-336 in LLaVA-1.5-7B; SigLIP ViT-B/16-384 in LLaVA-1.5; SigLIP-so400m in LLaVA-OneVision-7B (Qwen2)
main_result: LLaVA-1.5-7B: DyMU-low keeps 89 +/- 27 of 576 visual tokens (-84.5%) at 97.5% of the baseline's average score over 9 benchmarks (61.5 vs 63.1); DyMU-high 394 +/- 57 tokens at 63.2
notes: DToMe = ToMe's bipartite matching on keys inside the vision encoder, but edges are kept when their similarity exceeds a per-layer threshold tau_i instead of taking the top r, so the number of visual tokens varies with image complexity; the thresholds are calibrated once, without training, by ranking edges over large batches of 250k images so that B*r_i edges are merged on average per layer. Virtual Token Unmerging reconstructs the full-length RoPE attention inside the LLM from the merged tokens plus a position map. No parameters, no fine-tuning. Evaluated only on VLM/video benchmarks, no DeiT-S or ImageNet. Only FLOPs of the attention block are given (Table 1) and the paper notes the wall-clock difference is marginal with PyTorch attention. Code via project page only.
evidence: "Dynamic Token Merging (DToMe) reduces the number of visual token embeddings by merging similar tokens based on image complexity" (Abstract); "We then apply a threshold tau_i to retain edges t -> t_B where S_i [t] > tau_i . main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.9 at 3.0 GFLOPs (reduction 30% at layers 4, 7, 10; baseline 79.8 at 4.6), 3659 img/s vs 2803 for DeiT-S on an RTX 4090 FP32
notes: At layers 4, 7, 10 the attention map is split into a low-pass part (1/n)11^T and a high-pass remainder; the tokens with the largest column weight in the high-pass attention (70% kept, tau=0.3 reduction) are preserved as high-frequency tokens and the remaining low-frequency tokens are averaged into w^2 local DC tokens (w = 2, 1, 1) that are carried forward, so dropped tokens are fused rather than discarded; attention is rescaled with two learnable per-head weights omega1, omega2. Fine-tuned 30 epochs with self-distillation from the original model. Table 1 reports 79.8% and labels the cost MACs (3.0), while Table 3 reports 79.9% and labels the same configuration 3.0 GFLOPs; Table 5 pairs 79.9% with 3659 img/s. Appendix Table 3 gives a searched Pareto configuration (2.6 GFLOPs, 79.6). Throughput on an RTX 4090, FP32, batch size not stated; FlashAttention-compatible variant also timed.
evidence: "Our method partitions tokens into high-frequency tokens and low-frequency tokens. high-frequency tokens are selectively preserved, while low-frequency tokens are aggregated into a compact direct current token to retain essential low-frequency components." name: RAPID
backbones: DeiT-B; ViT-B; ViT-L (timm, ImageNet-1k pretrained); DeiT-S
main_result: DeiT-B off-the-shelf, r=14 (29 output tokens): top-1 80.52 at 3052 img/s (full model 81.97 at 1938 img/s; ToMe 79.42, ToFu 80.23); DeiT-S 79.57 at a 35% compression rate (ToMe 79.25, ToFu 79.08)
notes: A fixed r tokens removed per layer. In layers 1-4 the source tokens (bipartite split by index) with the highest redundancy score sum_j max(s_ij - tau, 0) over cosine similarities to destination tokens (tau = 0.7) are pruned; from layer 5 on, source tokens are merged into their best destination using similarity minus lambda times the shortfall of their CLS attention below the top-20% cutoff (lambda = 50). Plug-and-play, no training. For DeiT-S only accuracy at '35% compression rate' (percentage of retained output tokens) is given, no FLOPs or throughput. Throughput (synthetic 224px inputs, AMP FP16, batch 64) on a single RTX 4090 for DeiT-B, ViT-B and ViT-L; RAPID is slightly slower than ToMe/ToFu at the same r. ToFu baseline re-implemented by the authors. Undergraduate consortium paper (KDD 2026).
evidence: "in shallow-to-middle layers, RAPID employs a redundancy-similarity aware pruning metric to eliminate over-represented local patterns. As features transition to global semantic concepts in deeper layers, the framework shifts to an importance-similarity aware merging mechanism. This stage leverages classification (CLS) token attention weights to protect semantically critical tokens" (Abstract); "the method first takes as input the number of tokens to be reduced at each layer, denoted by r" (Sec. 3.1); "Our framework provides a training-free template for optimizing vision models" (Abstract)

name: G2TM
backbones: ViT-T/S/B/L (AugReg, 384px classification); Segmenter-T/S/B/L (Linear and Mask Transformer); SETR-B/L (Naive, PUP, MLA); EoMT-L (AugReg and DINOv2)
main_result: ViT-S (AugReg, 384px, 576 tokens): top-1 82.8 at 12.07 GFLOPs with G2TM at block 2 (baseline 83.0 at 15.52 GFLOPs); Seg-L Mask Transformer on ADE20K: mIoU 52.0 at 284.6 GFLOPs, 20.4 FPS (baseline 52.3, 400.1 GFLOPs, 14.9 FPS)
notes: A single merging step after the attention of block 1 or 2: a 4-neighbour graph over patch tokens weighted by cosine similarity is cut at a threshold tau (0.86-0.95), each connected component is averaged into one token, so the token count varies per image; the stored indices are used to unmerge (copy back) before dense decoders. Fine-tuned with masked attention and a threshold curriculum (G2TM dagger); Tables 7-8 give off-the-shelf results (small drop for classification, larger for segmentation). Throughput is the median FPS at batch size 1 on an A100 80GB. Classification uses AugReg ViT at 384px, so no DeiT-S. The abstract says 'Codes are available here' but the link target is not present in the text. G2TM was introduced in the authors' earlier Segmenter paper [41]; this paper is the systematic study.
